title: split-fused-qkv-kernel-and-rope-swap-prefetch-scheduler
author: Evan Park
description: Motivation: reduce tail latency and improve per-GPU throughput for common small-batch streaming workloads by separating concerns in the attention path. This PR decouples the fused QKV arithmetic from rotary/rope application and introduces a lightweight rope-swap stage plus a GPU-side KV prefetch streamer integrated with the continuous-batching scheduler. Rationale: tightly fused QKV+rotary kernels are fast on steady, large-batch workloads but cause memory layout churn and head-of-line blocking for bursty single-request streams and mixed sequence lengths. By splitting the fused kernel and moving rotary application to a deterministic post-QKV pass we can reuse packed QKV buffers across nearby requests and prefetch remote KV shards before decode starts. What this PR does: 1) Introduces a new tiled QKV kernel (FlashLoop wrapper) that focuses exclusively on Q/K/V matmuls and packing; it accepts an optional packed-output flag so the scheduler can keep buffers GPU-resident for a short window. 2) Adds a rope-swap stage (device and CPU fallbacks) that applies rotary/rope in-place or in a streaming chunked mode for very long sequences. 3) Implements a KV prefetch streamer in the continuous-batching scheduler that issues async copies for predicted hot KV shards while request tokens are being decoded; integrates with the existing cache eviction heuristics. 4) Adds runtime toggles and telemetry for the new stages (opt-in via config and feature flag for canary customers). Backwards compatibility: default behavior on main is unchanged until feature-flag rollout completes; new kernel is gated by runtime config so we can A/B or do canary rollouts. Testing: unit tests for kernel correctness (compare against fused QKV+rotary baseline), integration tests for scheduler prefetch logic, and microbench harness results included below. Benchmarks (A100, fp16, seq=1024 unless noted): - Small-batch streaming (batch=1, token-by-token): p50 latency down 7%, p95 down 14%, end-to-end throughput up 8-12% depending on model width. - Mixed-batch steady-state (batch 8-16): throughput neutral to +3% (depends on quantization path). - KV-heavy rerank workload (large cache churn): effective GPU utilization improved by ~15% due to prefetch overlap. - Worst-case long-seq (seq>8192): rope-swap chunked path shows 10% lower memory overhead vs fused kernel. CI notes: one flaky integration test (scheduler/eviction_test) failed on first run, was rerun and passed; no test regressions after fixes. Rollback plan: toggle feature-flag to false and revert canary pool; kernel code is additive and default path unchanged. Risks and mitigations: slight increase in code surface for kernel staging; mitigated by conservative defaults, telemetry, and canary rollout. Release notes: improved small-batch streaming latency and KV-heavy workload throughput via new split-QKV kernel and rope-swap prefetching. Additional context and links: Linear ENG-3789 for rollout plan, perf-canary dashboards attached in the PR comments.
